title: Habitat Schoolhouse Preschool Workbook 2 — Part 1 (Letters E, F + Earth/Ocean Theme)
publisher: The Habitat Schoolhouse Inc / Gumboot Kid

newActivityTypes.description: Full-page watercolor Earth illustration with labeled parts: North Pole, South Pole, Equator, Northern Hemisphere, Southern Hemisphere, Ocean, Land, Clouds. Below: 'How many poles does the earth have?' (dot-trace number 2) + 'The Earth is the ___ planet from the Sun' (multiple choice: First/Third/Tenth).
newActivityTypes.recipeNote: NEW — a labeled diagram page combining science vocabulary, counting, and comprehension questions. More advanced than the WB5 animal anatomy pages because it introduces geographic/scientific terminology.

newActivityTypes.description: Letter Ff themed: 'Fish — Animal Study on Tuna Fish.' Full Q&A format: What does a tuna fish look like? What do they like to eat? What is a tuna's habitat? What are tuna fish good at? Watercolor illustrations of two tuna species. This is a READ-ALOUD nonfiction page — the parent reads the questions and answers to the child.
newActivityTypes.skill: science (marine biology), reading comprehension, vocabulary, scientific questioning
newActivityTypes.recipeNote: NEW — a structured nonfiction read-aloud page with Q&A format. Teaches scientific questioning patterns (What does it look like? What does it eat? Where does it live? What is it good at?).

comparisonToOtherWorkbooks.vsWB1: WB1 was all sensory/kinesthetic (playdough, paint, placing objects). WB2 adds nonfiction reading and scientific diagrams. Cognitive demands are increasing.
comparisonToOtherWorkbooks.vsWB5: WB5 had simple animal anatomy diagrams (labeled body parts). WB2 has both anatomy AND geographic/astronomical diagrams (labeled Earth). WB2 also has full nonfiction read-aloud pages (animal studies) that WB5 didn't have.
comparisonToOtherWorkbooks.progression: WB1 (hands-on) → WB2 (hands-on + early nonfiction reading + diagrams) → WB5 (all activity types + more complex sorting). The series builds a reading-for-information habit very early.

gaps.name: labeled-science-diagram
gaps.description: A watercolor illustration of a scientific subject (Earth, solar system, animal, plant) with labeled parts pointing to key features. Below: counting question (dot-trace) + comprehension question (multiple choice). Combines science vocabulary, spatial reasoning, counting, and reading.

gaps.name: animal-study-nonfiction-page
gaps.description: A structured Q&A nonfiction page about an animal: What does it look like? What does it eat? What is its habitat? What is it good at? Watercolor illustrations. Designed as a read-aloud — parent reads to child. Teaches scientific questioning patterns.

notes: Thirteenth Aless drop. Third Habitat Schoolhouse workbook (WB1, WB2, WB5 now in the collection). WB2 introduces two significant new activity types: labeled science diagrams (Earth with geographic terms) and nonfiction animal study pages (Q&A format). This shows the series isn't just letter-of-the-week — it integrates science, geography, and nonfiction reading from Workbook 2 onward. The watercolor art quality is consistently museum-grade.
